column2: btrfs-vol -b would break any COW links

column1: on data blocks or metadata.  This was slow and caused the amount

The new code can keeps the sharing of all data extents and
most of the tree blocks.
To maintain the sharing of data extents
a seperate inode hold data extent pointers
to point to the new location.
To maintain the sharing of tree blocks
reloc trees to relocate tree blocks in reference counted roots.
There is one reloc tree for each subvol
same root key objectid. Reloc trees are snapshots of the latest
committed roots of subvols (root->commit_root).
To relocate a tree block referenced by a subvol
COW the block through subvol's reloc tree
the subvol to point to the new block. Since all reloc trees share
same root key objectid
column2: doing special handing for tree blocks

column1: owned by them is easy. Once a tree block has been COWed in one
reloc tree
column2: we can use the resulting new block directly when the

column1: same block is required to COW again through other reloc trees.

column2: relocated tree blocks are shared between reloc trees
